The decay

Series J: a neutron family becoming another by the transformation become, the products' flight to the shell, the W exchange at one Link.

A registered world, examples/events/weak/j3_neutron_free.json, run as it is declared; its register entry is J, the weak force (2026-09-20). Nothing was changed in the world and nothing is pinned by this page.

Also registered here and run as declared: examples/events/weak/j3_deuteron.json and examples/events/weak/w_exchange.json. The counts and the trigger ticks are the register's (the series README, weak/expectations.json).

The GameBoard

J3, the neutron's decay against its clock. An open cube of 21 x 21 x 21, K = 1 048 576, N = 64, release [1, 1], suspension [1, 2^20]. The neutron is a free body of 1839 units of n at (10, 10, 10) with the transformation become at 512 into p with the products beta (1 unit of content 3, the charge -7344 per unit of amount) and nu (1 unit of content 0): at the self-creation whose clock reaches 512 the event becomes a proton and the products are born as a re-release is, with the recoil over both. A shell of 762 measured events of the paid family d at r = 8 is one beam detector shell measuring beta with reads age (the flight time on the click) and passing everything else. In j3_deuteron the neutron is bound to a proton at one Link (series I's deuteron, the strong column G = 10 000, lifetime 3, the width 2^28) and its clock is slowed by the count it reads, the crowd of the proton's rows. The W exchange. A bar of 7 x 1 x 1: the neutron fixed at x = 2 with become at 8 into p with the one product w (1 unit of content 3, the paid family with the whole charge -7344 per unit of amount and the lifetime 1) on the direction +x, the proton of 1836 fixed at x = 3.

Why this page

The owner asked to see a family becoming another. In this law the weak force is not a coupling but a rule on the one-way side of the border: a measured event of one family becomes an event of another at the self-creation whose clock reaches a declared key, the rest released as products with the recoil, the charges balancing at load; the clock is slowed by the count it reads as every clock is, so a neutron in a crowd fires later and a neutron alone at the key exactly. The hand of the products (series P, the parity test) and the neutrino's phase window (series J2, the filter) are cited below from the register; this page shows the transformation itself.

The free neutron

What to see: nothing for 511 intervals but the neutron's own rows; at 512 the become line: the neutron becomes a proton, the beta (content 3) leaves on (1, 3, -2) and the neutrino on (1, 3, -1), the recoil (-70, -211, 121) on the new proton; the beta clicks the shell at the interval 526 at (12, 17, 6) with the content 3 (the register: one click, the content 3); the neutrino, a free row of content 0, passes every reader and leaves through a face (nu through face:+y at 533).

The bound neutron

What to see: the same key, later. The neutron's clock counts the proton's crowd at one Link (the count read at the trigger 128 590), so the transformation fires at 568 (the register under the fraction-free law: 568; the free neutron's 512); the beta clicks the shell at 581 with the content 3; the pair is then two protons at one Link and holds (0 steps of 64 attempted, every attempt a hand-over). Against nature the register states the law's own prediction: a bound neutron that decays later where nature's is stable by its binding energy.

The W exchange at one Link

What to see: at the interval 8 the neutron becomes a proton and throws the W on +x with the recoil (-192, 0, 0); at ? the proton one Link away measures it (the click, the push ?) and has afterwards the charge [0, 1] and the content 1 839: a neutron's, in the detector's terms. No W reaches the border lifetime. The exchange is complete at the click; the momenta (-192, 0, 0) and (192, 0, 0).
